speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. To help assess your newborn's jaundice, I need to know the baby's gestational age and exact age in hours or days. Has the baby been feeding well, and have you noticed any dark urine or pale stools?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-week-old female newborn. The patient has been experiencing increasing yellow discoloration of her eyes and skin for 2 days. She was born at 39 weeks' gestation, initially weighed 3066 g and now weighs 3200 g. The patient is exclusively breastfed.

speaker: Doctor
text: Is the infant feeding well and having adequate wet diapers? REQUEST TEST: Total_Bilirubin_and_Direct_Bilirubin

speaker: Doctor
text: The labs indicate unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia, which is common in breastfed infants. I need to check for signs of hemolysis or infection, so please confirm if there are any visible bruises, birthmarks, or family history of blood disorders. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal hematocrit suggests no significant hemolysis. Are there any other family members with a history of jaundice or thyroid issues, and has the baby had a newborn screening test yet? REQUEST TEST: Thyroid_Stimulating_Hormone_TSH

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal TSH and CBC effectively rule out hemolysis and hypothyroidism as causes for this unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia. This clinical picture is most consistent with breast milk jaundice, a benign condition often seen in exclusively breastfed infants around two weeks of age. DIAGNOSIS READY: Breast milk jaundice
